Arsenal face January dilemma as Liverpool and Chelsea join Alex Scott transfer race

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (547 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readarsenal

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a potential move for Alex Scott.
  • According to The i Paper, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all made exploratory enquiries about the 23-year-old.
  • Arsenal are believed to be keen on a summer move.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a potential move for Alex Scott. Mikel Arteta may have to rethink his transfer prepares if competition for the midfielder intensifies.

According to The i Paper, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all made exploratory enquiries about the 23-year-old. The clubs want to establish what it would take to persuade Bournemouth to sell. However, none appears close to agreeing to a deal.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on a summer move. Liverpool and Chelsea are more interested in signing Scott in January. However, if they were to make a serious offer, it could be hard to hold out.

Scott has become one of the most exciting midfielders in the Premier League. He is an attractive option for clubs looking to improve their squad going forward due to his age, experience and being a homegrown player.

However, there is some uncertainty around Scott’s future. The England international has turned down two contract offers and is unwilling to sign a upcoming deal. There are 18 months left on Scott’s contract, meaning it is an increasingly important decision for Bournemouth.

Arsenal are interested in Scott with doubts surrounding their own midfield options. There have been reports linking Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino to exits.

Scott would give Arteta another option, but Arsenal will have to consider if they want to make a move and give Liverpool and Chelsea an advantage.

Bournemouth are reported to want more than £100m to let him go during the January transfer window.

Sources indicate that it would be a big asking price, especially given that Scott has 18 months left on his contract. There are a few reasons why Bournemouth could be holding out for a big fee.

The Cherries had to pay £25m to bring Scott in from Bristol City, who will receive 20 per cent of any future transfer fee. They will also have to find a suitable replacement at the halfway stage.

Reports said Chelsea received a number of offers worth around £70m in the summer, but Bournemouth have rejected claims that a bid of £80m will get them talking.

Scott is believed to be happy to stay at the club until the end of the campaign. Bournemouth are also having a great season under Marco Rose, currently sitting in seventh place in the Premier League with eight straight wins in all competitions.

Industry observers note that arsenal have little to hurry into any deal and could use the summer to negotiate a better deal. This is especially true with Scott’s contract situation becoming more of an problem.

The problem is that Liverpool and Chelsea are keen competitors and could lead to a bidding war in January, leaving Arsenal with little room to negotiate.

It has been revealed that whilst Arsenal have made their interest known, this doesn’t necessarily mean he will be moving anytime soon. If Scott is a genuine target, then they must be prepared to pounce if the situation arises.

The Newcastle United stars in international action this month.

Great to see some excellent performances from United players.

So far, a perfect record of seven wins out of seven in this international break.

The senior international matches when Newcastle United players have played a part.

Yoane Wissa kicked things off with right foot volley to set DR Congo on their way to victory over Sierra Leone on Thursday.

That same day United teenager Ousmane Diabate played the full match as Guinea won an AFCON qualifier against Eritrea.

A perfect Thursday was completed when Dan Burn and Lewis Hall both excelled as England defeated Croatia 2-1 at Wembley to make it three wins out of three for Newcastle’s internationals this month.

Friday we saw Malick Thiaw make his third start in a row under Jurgen Klopp as Germany won 3-1 away in Serbia.

Moving on to Saturday and William Osula came off the bench to help Denmark to a stunning 4-1 away win over Portugal.

The same night Anthony Elanga created the opening goal as Sweden won 3-2 in a thriller against Bosnia & Herzegovina (Newcastle’s Amar Dedic was on the losing side but then it was impossible for both teams to win…).

Then on Sunday night a magnificent 3-2 England victory in Madrid. Lewis Hall playing the full match and excellent, whilst Dan Burn came off the bench to help see out this famous victory over Spain.

Monday will see Malick Thiaw potentially line up for a fourth start in a row for Jurgen Klopp as Germany take on the Netherlands.

Then on Tuesday, up to six different senior internationals will see Newcastle United stars on the pitch.

This is the November 2026 international schedule for Newcastle United players:.

DR Congo 3 Sierra Leone 1 Yoane Wissa volleying home after 189 seconds for a 9th goal in his last 13 internationals, a 3-1 final scoreline in this AFCON qualifying group win.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Viktor Gyökeres has put to bed any doubts over his future at Arsenal by stating his desire to stay.
  • In a recent development, the striker has been under question over his long-term future under Mikel Arteta after a difficult start to the 2026/27 season.
  • Sources indicate that gyökeres moved to Arsenal for £63.5m from Sporting Lisbon last summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Viktor Gyökeres has put to bed any doubts over his future at Arsenal by stating his desire to stay.

In a recent development, the striker has been under question over his long-term future under Mikel Arteta after a difficult start to the 2026/27 season. His latest comments suggest he will not be seeking a move away from north London.

Sources indicate that gyökeres moved to Arsenal for £63.5m from Sporting Lisbon last summer. He’s played a key role in the club winning the Premier League last season with 14 league goals.

However, he has not featured as much this season. Kai Havertz often being Arteta’s go-to man centrally, resulting in him only starting once in the Premier League.

In a recent development, this has led to some speculation that the Sweden international may look at his options in January. However, his latest interview with the Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen suggests otherwise.

Gyökeres was asked if he wants to stay at Arsenal and has made it clear he wants to continue his career at the Emirates.

The striker also spoke about his relationship with Arteta.

It has been revealed that he explained that they regularly discuss football, the team’s approach and the opposition. Those conversations also help him understand what Arteta expects when he is selected to start.

It is a key point to note that just because he hasn’t had much time on the pitch doesn’t mean there have been any challenges between the two.

In a recent development, gyökeres has begun to show his worth again in recent weeks. He found the net against Fleetwood in the League Cup and then Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

This came after a long time to get his first goal of the season and gives him the chance to remind Arteta what he can bring to the team.

There is no doubt that Gyökeres has not lived up to the expectations he had when he came from Portugal.

According to recent reports, but his overall effect cannot be ignored. He has contributed 23 goals and 6 assists in 69 games for Arsenal.

The challenge will be finding a way to get the best out of him and Havertz. They add different attributes, and Arteta will have plenty of options to choose from depending on the opposition.

They will also want to avoid losing someone they have invested heavily in so early on. Gyökeres has a contract until 2030, so they are in a great position.

His latest comments will help to reassure fans that he is not looking to leave the club after stating his ambition to play more games and make himself an indispensable part of Arteta’s squad.

The main thing for Arsenal will be to make sure that he can turn this attitude into consistent performances. Gyökeres has made his intentions clear and now needs to show why they brought him to North London in the first place.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A failed transfer bid from the summer had looked to be back on West Ham’s radar for Nils Koppen to revisit when the window opens for business in the next few weeks: Transfer talks in August between West Ham and Nürnburg proved fruitless – despite the Hammers reported £17 million bid – for striker Mohamed Ali Zoma.

The player was said to be hugely keen on the move but his club refused to sanction the deal that would have brought the 20-goal Bundesliga 2 talent to West Ham.

The Hammers settled on Joel Piroe instead, but were apparently hankering after another crack at signing Ali Zoma in January.

However there seems another fly in the ointment which could well prove a latest stumbling block. This was a significant milestone in his first season with the Arsenal team, and he has since remained as number one, playing a key role in the club’s pursuit of titles.

The match ending Spain 2 England 3 but that only tells a very small part of the story.

England by a huge distance the better team and going 3-0 up in less than an hour, it should have been more.

Spain massively got away with one as moments of madness from Jarell Quansah, Elliot Anderson and Anthony Gordon, threatened to destroy what had been a supreme team performance.

With England so much on top, their individual errors in a 12 minute second half spell directly led to the two undeserved Spanish goals and Thomas Tuchel’s team having to play the final 30 or so minutes a man down.

Somebody who didn’t put a foot wrong was Lewis Hall.

We have to now pay tribute and give our thanks to those in the media who have now suddenly ‘discovered’ the brilliant 22-year-old.

I wonder what lifelong Newcastle United fan Lewis Hall has been up to these last few years…?

Lamine Yamal had played in 32 competitive matches for Spain, where they had won 27 of them, drawing five and losing none.

Then the winger ran into Lewis Hall, again.

Lamine Yamal losing in his 33rd competitive appearance for Spain, his first ever.

The only surprise about this Lamine Yamal v Lewis Hall contest was that anybody should be surprised.

It was only in March this year that the pair were up against each other when Newcastle United hosted Barcelona at St James’ Park, Lewis Hall up against Lamine Yamal.

Lamine Yamal scored a fortunate late equaliser from the penalty spot, however, there was no doubt about who won this duel of top class winger and elite lifelong Newcastle United fan.

Barcelona star man Lamine Yamal wasn’t able to dribble past Lewis Hall even once in the 90+ minutes. Whilst the United defender was superb going forward, creating five chances, the most created by any player on the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that on top of all of that, the appalling referee failed to book Lamine Yamal for a cynical foul on Lewis Hall, after yet again the NUFC player got the better of him. A yellow card which would have been Yamal’s third in the competition and seen him suspended for the second leg.

Last night in Madrid was very reminiscent of St James’ Park in March, the only joy Lamine Yamal got was when he was marked by somebody else out wide, or when he came inside to get away from Lewis Hall. Plus of course those two awful errors from Quansah and Gordon that led to the Spanish goals.

It was also amusing to see once again last night, what happens when things go against a young prima donna such as Lamine Yamal. His diving was so impressive and his petulance was a joy to see as he reacted to Hall and England’s dominance with fouls of his own as things weren’t going his and Spain’s way.

Lamine Yamal is an exciting talent.

Lewis Hall though is even better.

There must be a sense of disappointment amongst West Ham’s academy that one of their much-heralded strikers, poached from north of the border in July 2025, hasn’t yet progressed on a more impressive trajectory.

After all, Daniel Cummings joined West Ham as the latest nineteen year old striker ‘wonderkid’ with Champions League experience having featured in Celtic’s European campaign before quitting the club and heading for east London last summer.

Sending the young forward out on loan to fifth-tier Aldershot Town (no disrespect to Aldershot) could be seen as West Ham’s tacit admission that the striker has not yet delivered on the precocious talent he displayed in Celtic’s youth team scoring, seemingly, at will.

After all, West Ham academy contemporary Josh Landers headed on loan to Scottish Championship side Ayr United – not exactly the Premier League either – but more challenging surely than the Vanarama National League in which Cummings now finds himself.

Fellow academy Scot Josh Landers is at Ayr United on loan.

Of course, there’s a certain amount of schadenfreude from his old club. Celtic fan site celticshorts.com proclaim with glee the apparent stalling of Cummings’ progress:.

“Grass is seldom greener after leaving Celtic – Daniel Cummings heads to Aldershot Town…From playing in Champions League at Villa Park for Celtic to Aldershot Town”.

Which Cummings will just have to deal with, get his head down, score some goals and answer the criticism from his former club in the best possible way.

In case they hadn’t noticed, now more than ever there’s an opening back at home for any young striker who creates a splash and one or other of Landers or Cummings could easily find themselves recalled after a prolific, headline-making few months.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

According to recent reports, admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

According to recent reports, but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

It has been revealed that the Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Recent findings suggest that keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews stated. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

Brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

According to recent reports, any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very important points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola stated they will now be out “for some time”.

Sources indicate that the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” stated Iraola.

Recent findings suggest that the injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa mentioned: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

Keith Andrews has established a clearly defined, direct style of play which speaks to Brentford’s strengths. His side are third in the Premier League for percentage of passes forward (39.2 per cent) and, coupled with the second-most high turnovers which end in a goal, Brentford have thrived off passages of organised chaos.

To play this way requires quality when you do have the ball, and full-backs Keane Lewis-Potter and Michael Kayode deserve particular praise. They have contributed materially to Brentford’s attacks, helping their side to league-high successful crosses (26) and expected goals from set-pieces (4.03).

Sources indicate that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca stated in his pre-match press conference.”.

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”.

Ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

Elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be said for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

Sources indicate that pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The value of international friendlies has always seemed questionable mid season: During a challenging domestic schedule the disruption of thousands of miles of travel, different coaching regimes and playing styles can easily prove disruptive: Let alone the risk of injuries to jaded players.

West Ham United have their fair share of absentees on international duty right now, which Scott Parker must be rueing as he tries to rebuild the playing style of the squad he has inherited from his predecessor.

However there’s an upside to  those international fixtures if it allows squad members to improve their game and their confidence – and several of the Hammers’ squad will come back to their club in far better spirits than they left.

As we covered yesterday Mads Hermansen’s headline winning performance to keep out Portugal can only have done him good.

International debut for Hammers youngster Mohamadou Kanté.

Mohamadou Kanté must be made up at making his international debut for Mali – on the winning side in his first time wearing the national shirt means the midfield man will come back with a little more of a swagger than he left with, whilst news of Joel Piroe’s brace on international duty for Suriname will have been similarly well received at Rush Green.

With Castellanos and Pablo misfiring so badly, much is expected of the on-loan Leeds man and for Piroe to grab two goals in his national side’s 4-0 victory over Eswatini (formerly Swaziland, for anyone else who wondered) can only be a confidence boost for West Ham’s number nine ahead of the resumption of the Championship at the weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan Shearer believes Ezri Konsa has been the Premier League’s best player this season after an impressive start to his Arsenal career.

But the former Newcastle United striker has been impressed by the Gunners’ backline and feels Konsa should take a large amount of credit for the fact that they have not missed William Saliba so much.

According to recent reports, konsa’s arrival at Emirates has provided Mikel Arteta with a defender, but his performances have caused some challenges for the Arsenal boss. Konsa is now a viable option for Arteta to play, as Saliba is fit again.

Shearer feels Konsa has done enough to be regarded as the best player in the division so far.

He stated in the Metro that Konsa has been effective while playing for Arsenal in the defence.

The former Newcastle player believed that Konsa has been the best player in the Premier League during this season. He pointed out the proof of the performance in the defence, arguing that people did not notice the missing Saliba until now.

Konsa has proved just how much he has grown since moving to the Emirates. Arsenal have been very strong at the back with Konsa playing a massive part.

But there is a problem with Konsa’s performances. Even if Saliba is fit he has done more than enough to make his place difficult to take.

Sources indicate that saliba is still one of Arsenal’s most important defenders, so Arteta will be delighted to have him back. However, he can’t ignore what Konsa has done in his absence.

Industry observers note that it would be a tough call to leave the Englishman out, as he has been in such great form. But it means an experienced first choice defender would be left on the bench.

Konsa and Saliba could make a good partnership if they are given time to understand each other on the pitch. They will need to play regularly to do this.

According to recent reports, konsa has made it very hard not to pick him. He has been performing so well that he has created a dilemma for the manager.

In a recent development, shearer highlights how well he has done by saying this. Arteta will have to figure out how to make the most out of his two quality defenders.

Ben White returned to the England senior squad on Thursday night but received a hostile reception at Wembley.

The Arsenal defender came on as a substitute in the 78th minute of England’s 2-1 Nations League win against Croatia but was met with boos from a section of the crowd.

Recent findings suggest that thomas Tuchel has since defended White, stating that he should be in the squad. However, this raises questions as to why some England supporters have turned on the defender after he has continued to perform well for Arsenal.

The answer lies with the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

It has been revealed that white left the England World Cup camp in November 2022, returning home due to personal reasons. The FA confirmed that White will not return to the squad and asked that his privacy be respected.

He did not play in the first two group games for England and missed the last group game against Wales due to illness.

There were reports that White had fallen out with assistant manager Steve Holland, but neither the FA nor England management confirmed this was the reason he left.

Gareth Southgate later stated there were no problems between White and Holland and that White had simply withdrawn himself from selection after the tournament.

Recent findings suggest that this meant that White would never play for England again while Southgate was still manager. Some fans were clearly upset by this, as they felt White was shunning his country.

In a recent development, when White returned under Tuchel in March 2026, he was met with a negative reaction. He was booed by the crowd when he scored his first-ever international goal against Uruguay. White was also booed in the same fashion against Japan.

He has since explained that supporters might view the situation differently if they knew the full story. However, he has chosen not to reveal the private details behind his departure.

Tuchel has shown little concern about White being affected by the controversy.

The England boss noted after the win on Thursday that he had not heard any boos and praised White’s qualities, work ethic and desire to play for his country.

He believes White can help England win games and added that he has the backing of the coaching staff.

Arsenal fans will be unsurprised to learn that White is still a valuable asset for Mikel Arteta, offering defensive consistency and being able to play as a right or centre-back.

The bad press that White is receiving from England fans will not go away any time soon. However, he has not done anything to hurt his reputation at club level. The reasons why he left for the World Cup are personal.

Industry observers note that the main focus for Arsenal will be getting him match fit again. As for the England fans, we shall see.

#2358. For Newcastle United these are now the steps that matter

For Newcastle United these are now the steps that matter

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (998 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are Newcastle United seasons that announce themselves with the flourish of a fanfare, and there are seasons that arrive more quietly, almost tentatively, as if testing the ground beneath their feet.
  • This one, for Newcastle United, belongs firmly to the latter category.
  • Ten Premier League matches into the 2026-27 campaign, the Magpies sit in twelfth place with twelve points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are Newcastle United seasons that announce themselves with the flourish of a fanfare, and there are seasons that arrive more quietly, almost tentatively, as if testing the ground beneath their feet.

This one, for Newcastle United, belongs firmly to the latter category.

Ten Premier League matches into the 2026-27 campaign, the Magpies sit in twelfth place with twelve points. Three victories, three draws, four defeats.

Industry observers note that the numbers are neither catastrophic nor comforting. They are, instead, the arithmetic of transition.

After years of ascent under Eddie Howe—punctuated by European nights and the rare, precious taste of silverware—the club has entered a deliberate, if painful, period of reconstruction. Key figures have departed. Younger, less seasoned players have arrived. And into this unsettled landscape has stepped Matthias Jaissle, a thoughtful German coach still learning the particular cadences of the Premier League. Let’s pray he is precocious!

The style he favors—“vertical football”—is direct, urgent, and ambitious. Yet in these early weeks it has often looked unfinished, like a promising manuscript that still requires careful editing. Attacks break down before they fully form. The midfield sometimes lacks the necessary ballast. Set-pieces, once a source of both goals and defensive security, have lost their edge. Chance creation has been modest. The underlying numbers suggest a side that is still searching for its rhythm.

Industry observers note that I would argue that the back half of last season under Eddie Howe, and with the “superstars” who moved on to their perceived “bigger” clubs, the performances were no better. I flew 3,500 miles to attend the Bournemouth match – at great expense may I add – to witness the worst Newcastle United performance in my near 50 years of following the club. The rot started last season (and I would venture to say in the summer of 2025).

Recent findings suggest that none of this should surprise those who have followed the club’s longer story. Newcastle has always been a place where ambition and constraint exist in uneasy conversation. The Saudi ownership brought resources and expectation, but the financial rules of the modern game impose their own discipline, that I wish would be challenged in court as anti-competitive.

The past 2026 summer window reflected that reality: significant investment, yes, but also the departure of established leaders (good riddance to the rats!) and the calculated gamble on potential rather than proven readiness.

Still, there are concrete steps available this season—practical, unglamorous steps that can steady the ship without pretending the rebuild is already complete.

Matthias Jaissle must first allow himself the freedom of pragmatism. The purest version of his vertical approach has, at times, left the team exposed and the attack under-supplied. A measured adjustment—greater control in build-up when the high press is broken, tighter rest defence, a clearer structure for the attacking midfielder—need not abandon the philosophy. It would simply make it sustainable. Restoring set-piece competence would be another quiet victory. These are matters of coaching detail, not revolution.

The Newcastle United squad itself still holds untapped value. Joelinton’s physical presence and ball-winning capacity remain essential once fully available, but we have a young gem in Sean Steur who, whilst not as physically imposing as Big Joe, is poised, creative, and doesn’t mind sticking a foot in. Dan Burn’s leadership and aerial strength can stabilise both ends of the pitch. The younger summer arrivals require patience but also clear pathways and honest assessment. A stable selection, built around those who are ready rather than those who might be ready later, would help establish the consistency that has been missing.

Then there is January. The winter window is rarely the stage for transformative spending at a club managing financial ratios carefully. Yet it can be the stage for precise, intelligent reinforcement. The most glaring absence is a natural number ten—a player capable of receiving between the lines, linking midfield to attack, and providing the creative spark that current options have not consistently delivered.

Recent findings suggest that one name that has already circulated is Bilal El Khannouss of Stuttgart. The Morocco international attacking midfielder was reportedly considered during the summer and is claimed to be available for a fee in the region of no more than£40 million, a figure that may prove more attainable than many alternatives. His profile—technical, progressive, comfortable in the half-spaces—aligns with what Jaissle appears to seek. Other options will be examined, of course. The market rarely offers perfect solutions in January. But the principle is clear: a ready-made creator who can accelerate the adaptation of the system would be more valuable than another project requiring time the club may not fully possess this season. Contract situations must also be addressed with clarity. Players entering the final year of their deals create both risk and opportunity. Selling at the right moment, rather than losing assets for nothing, can fund the necessary additions while maintaining squad balance.

None of this guarantees a return by Newcastle United to the higher reaches of the table overnight. That would be unrealistic. What it can provide is direction—a sense that the transition is being managed with purpose rather than simply endured. A top-half finish, or even a secure mid-table campaign accompanied by improved underlying performance, would represent genuine progress under the circumstances.

Football clubs, like the cities they represent, are defined as much by how they navigate difficulty as by how they celebrate success. Newcastle has known both extremes in recent years. The current chapter is quieter, more complicated, and less cinematic than the ones that preceded it. Yet it is no less consequential.

The work of improvement rarely arrives with trumpets. It arrives in adjustments of shape, in the careful acquisition of the right player at the right moment, and in the daily insistence that potential must eventually become performance. For Newcastle United this season, those are the steps that matter. The rest will follow, or it will not. But the path, at least, can be chosen with intention.

Despite the disappointing result against Portugal, it was a landmark evening for the Arsenal players.

Dowman is already building a legacy at club level, but now he can add to his list of records by becoming an England Under-21 record holder.

At just 16, he has plenty of time to improve and show consistent performances to get more opportunities with the senior Arsenal squad.
