📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 14 Nov 2026 22:11.

After claiming their first victory of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign in the opening leg at Essipong Sports Stadium, Ghana will be the nominal visitors when they face Somalia at the same venue in Monday afternoon's return fixture of their Group C double-header.

The Black Stars secured a 2-0 win when the sides met on Thursday, leaving them third in the section, six points behind leaders Ivory Coast, three adrift of second-placed Gambia and three ahead of Monday's designated hosts, who remain bottom without a point.

Ghana will be looking to record back-to-back victories for the first time in their qualifying campaign after a difficult start saw them lose to Ivory Coast and Gambia in September.

The Black Stars suffered a 2-0 defeat in Abidjan before surrendering a two-goal lead in a 4-2 home loss to Gambia, results that contributed to Carlos Queiroz's departure and left interim coach Kim Lars Bjorkegren with plenty of work to do.

Thursday's victory over Somalia offered some encouragement, with Jonas Adjetey opening the scoring shortly before halftime after Jordan Ayew had missed a penalty, before Felix Afena-Gyan added a second after the break.

The result also marked Bjorkegren's first competitive win in charge and Ghana's first AFCON qualifying victory in about three years, having missed out on the previous continental finals after a disappointing campaign.

Having also ended a five-match winless run last time out, the Black Stars will now be looking to secure consecutive victories for the first time since September and October 2025, with their only other win in their last 13 outings across all competitions coming against Panama in the World Cup group stage.

Somalia, meanwhile, have managed just one goal across their last six outings in all competitions, while losing each of their AFCON qualifying matches since progressing beyond the preliminary round with a penalty shootout victory over Mauritius.

Yusuf Ali Nur's team have conceded exactly twice in each of those qualifiers, losing 2-1 to Gambia in the opening round and 2-0 to Ivory Coast on matchday two before Thursday's defeat to Ghana.

Another loss on Monday would leave the Ocean Stars' hopes of reaching the continental finals for the first time hanging by a thread, with the side currently ranked a lowly 200th in the FIFA World Rankings facing a daunting task against opponents sitting 130 places higher.

There is little encouragement to draw from previous meetings, as Somalia have lost all three of their encounters with Ghana, conceding multiple goals each time while failing to find the net.

Somalia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Somalia form (all competitions):.

Ghana Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:.

Somalia have reported no new injury concerns or suspensions following the first meeting, and goalkeeper Ibrahim Ahmed Hussein could retain his place after saving Ayew's penalty.

Bilal Njie, Abel Gigli and Sakariya Hassan are among those who could feature again as Ali Nur looks for a stronger attacking performance.

Ghana will be without Antoine Semenyo and Jan Gyamerah, who are both unavailable through injury, while no suspensions have been confirmed.

Thomas Partey, Mohammed Kudus, Mohammed Salisu and captain Jordan Ayew all returned to the squad for the double-header, with the latter three expected to feature again after Thursday's victory.

Somalia possible starting lineup:.

Hussein; Mohamed, Gigli, Omar, Othman; Nour, Sharif, Abdullahi; Hassan, Moussa Njie, Bilal Njie.

Ghana possible starting lineup:.

Asare; Seidu, Adjetey, Salisu, Mensah; Partey, Yirenkyi; Fatawu, Kudus, Afena-Gyan; Ayew.

Somalia will be determined to improve on their performance from Thursday, but their lack of attacking threat in the first meeting makes it difficult to see them troubling Ghana over 90 minutes.

AC Milan are expected to hire Markus Krösche in the next few weeks, and a report has looked a little more at his work today.

Sources indicate that between Eintracht Frankfurt and Milan, there are plenty of differences. From the finances available to how they’re spent, even to the way in which the structure of the club ticks over. So, Krösche will have to learn with the Rossoneri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it won’t be a one way street, with the Diavolo needing to learn plenty too.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, Krösche methods are very linear; it’s about arriving and leaving at the right time, having the knowledge to enter and the courage to step away when the time is right.

His belief is that the club will always hold more weight than the manager, which has been shown in the past few months by Gerry Cardinale and there is no shortage of exciting signings on his CV.

What is also worth remembering is that he’s not one to step away from his methods. In 2022, he was given a chance to sign Cristiano Ronaldo. However, it didn’t make sense for him or Frankfurt, so they never made their move.

It has been revealed that if it happens his way, Timmo Hardung will arrive alongside the German. The pair met at RB Leipzig and their relationship has only grown since then and Krösche eventually led a team of 70 people at Frankfurt. In other words, he won’t be out of place at the top of the Milan football organisation.

Sources indicate that gazzetta even suggests that it’s ‘no secret’ that his desire is to move to Italy to work under Krösche once again. Given their successes together, it makes sense why all parties are hoping to keep that relationship under the same roof.

Mikel Merino is not an Arsenal starter, but even his role off the bench should come into question.

His latest performance for Spain has left plenty to be desired, with it being further proof that he is no longer good enough for the English champions.

The midfielder has struggled to make a consistent impact at club level, starting just one game in the Premier League this season, while featuring in all 10.

He has played just 203 minutes, but even then, he has not warranted his current level of appearances.

With Arsenal having plenty of options in midfield, Mikel Arteta must start questioning whether Merino deserves to remain part of his aims.

His latest numbers for Spain only add further weight to that argument.

Merino was handed a starting role in Spain's midfield but struggled to make any meaningful impact before being substituted at half-time.

With his season at Arsenal, it was a rare start for the Spaniard, but one he utterly failed to make the most of.

Against England, as per FotMob, Merino took just 20 touches in 45 minutes on the pitch, and it was no surprise to see him withdrawn after the first half.

Additionally, while he operated in a number 10 role, he did not get involved in the attacking play much.

He created just one chance - worth only 0.02 expected assists - and failed to get a shot of his own throughout the match, with his only attempt being blocked.

And he only had one touch in England's box throughout his performance, while being unsuccessful with his only attempted dribble - a zero per cent success rate.

Merino also only won one out of three ground duels, while he does deserve credit for his aerial presence with three out of four duels won there.

A performance lacking influence, a theme that has been commong for him at Arsenal.

Merino is only ever brought off the bench late on in games, with Arsenal looking to hold onto a lead.

That is clear, as he is averaging just 20.2 minutes per appearance.

It is likely down to his physicality, his 6'2" frame and his ability to play in numerous positions.

While his experience and versatility remain valuable, his limited involvement raises questions about his place in Arsenal's long-term plans.

And those are traits that can be easily replaced in the market, especially with someone who can have a bigger influence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rafael Benitez has opened up about the ‘difficult’ time that he had at Liverpool during the damaging ownership era of Tom Hicks and George Gillett.

The American businessmen bought the Merseyside club in 2007 amid grandiose promises about a fresh stadium in Stanley Park (‘a spade in the ground within 60 days’, and all that), but they quickly became hugely unpopular figures among the fan base.

As the duo ultimately fell out with one another amid a period of civil war at the club, debts mounted to the extent that LFC was on the brink of administration in 2010 before they were ousted by a takeover from New England Sports Ventures (now Fenway Sports Group).

In an interview with The Athletic, Benitez was asked if he ever thought back to what could’ve been for Liverpool had it not been for the damaging ownership of Hicks and Gillett, throughout which time the Spaniard kept the club challenging for major silverware.

The former Reds boss reflected: “Yes, 100%. When Hicks and Gillett came, they changed the approach. All the things you did for the benefit of the club, they had different ideas. I realised, and the fans realised later, that something was wrong. They didn’t have experience of football.

According to recent reports, “I remember speaking to Gillett once in London after we played Tottenham. He noted: ‘We will give you money and then next season you’ll get us into the play-offs.’ I had to tell him there were no play-offs.

“They thought maybe: ‘Rafa is a threat.’ That period was difficult, but all I ever wanted was the best for the club.”.

(Photo by Oli Scarff/Getty Images).

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Benitez’s final season at Liverpool in 2009/10 was a major disappointment, with the Reds expected to challenge for the title but slumping to a seventh-place finish, and there was a prevailing sentiment that the time was right for a change in the dugout.

However, as the extent of the damage done by Hicks and Gillett became clear in subsequent months and years, the latter part of the Spaniard’s managerial reign has come to be viewed in a much kinder light.

He was left with an impossible job of trying to achieve success on the pitch while all sorts of strife was going on in the background, slowly eating away at the club until John Henry rode to the rescue in October 2010.

Benitez’s time at Liverpool may have ended on a low ebb, but he remains a greatly appreciated figure among the fans for delivering Champions League glory in Istanbul and getting the Reds back to being a competitive force domestically and on the continent, even if the Premier League eluded him.

Had it not been for the incompetence of those at ownership level, who knows just how much more the Spaniard could’ve achieved at Anfield in the late 2000s and possibly into the 2010s?

The recent change in manager, with Mauricio Pochettino appointed to replace Michael Carrick, has led to suggestions of further upheaval within the squad at Old Trafford.

The 32-year-old's future has been a topic of discussion for months now, and there have been suggestions he could be tempted to quit in favour of a move elsewhere.

However, former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that he would be "very disappointed" to see Fernandes "jump ship" come the end of the season.

Instead, the captain has been called upon to help turn the club's recent forunes around, with his role as a key player on the pitch and leader in the dressing room set to be crucial.

Fernandes has less than a year remaining on his current contract, and could be tempted to leave for free, but Man United hold an option to extend which could still be triggered.

Football Insider revealed on 14 November that Pochettino is relying on Fernandes to help win over the Man United dressing room after reports of recent unrest.

Fernandes is among a number of star players who have spoken out about the situation behind the scenes, with the higher-ups and previous coaching staff under fire.

However, amidst all of the turmoil, Fernandes is being backed to aid the new manager in his position and has been called upon to help get things back on track at Man United.

"To put it quite bluntly, Bruno Fernandes has been nowhere near good enough this season," Brown told Football Insider.

Recent findings suggest that "We have to look at the situation as it is now, last season is gone, and he hasn't demonstrated up so far this season. He is as much to blame for this nightmare as anybody is.

"So now, I'm expecting him to step up as a leading influence in the dressing room and on the pitch and make sure things can be turned around.

"He's got to get behind the newly introduced manager, step up his performances, and work hard to get things moving in the right direction again.

"I would be very, very disappointed if he walked away now after the way he has performed and behaved this season, if he decided to jump ship and leave the club.

"He's the captain and he's going to have to play a crucial role in turning this season around, regardless of his contract situation which will be spoken about behind the scenes.".

Fernandes' contract situation has been a talking point behind the scenes at Old Trafford for at least 12 months now, with the player having already turned down moves away.

His role both on and off the pitch make him a vital asset for the Red Devils, who remain keen to keep him around, with suggestions that new contract talks have taken place.

Former Tottenham scout Bryan King told Football Insider on 22 October that Man United are hopeful that Fernandes will sign a latest deal to continue as their best player.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has mentioned: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died.

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch.

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'.

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono stated: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

Recent findings suggest that 'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many complications to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'.

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response.

Owono stated he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono).

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'.

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'.

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

'The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every one of the expressions of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of its heart, maximum respect for his privacy, in these terrible moments.'.

  • Lithuania welcome Liechtenstein to the Darius and Girenas Stadium on Monday evening for the final round of League D fixtures in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.
  • In their previous competition outing, Trispalves fell to a narrow 1-0 defeat against Azerbaijan, while Blau-Rot lost to Milli Komanda by the same scoreline on Friday evening.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Freddie Cotton | 14 Nov 2026 22:55.

Lithuania welcome Liechtenstein to the Darius and Girenas Stadium on Monday evening for the final round of League D fixtures in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Trispalves fell to a narrow 1-0 defeat against Azerbaijan, while Blau-Rot lost to Milli Komanda by the same scoreline on Friday evening.

After suffering relegation from League C in their 2024-25 Nations League endeavours, finishing bottom of Group 2 having failed to pick up a single point from their six matches, Lithuania will be fairly content with how they have performed in the competition over the previous few months.

Trispalves positively kick-started their campaign by beating Monday’s opposition away from home in their opening encounter before drawing with Azerbaijan, but after falling to a 1-0 defeat against the latter in their most recent outing, they are sat four points behind Odlar Yurdu, who have guaranteed top spot.

Alongside this, Lithuania also endured heartbreak in their latest pursuit of the Baltic Cup, as following a penalty shootout victory over Latvia in the semifinals, Trispalves conceded late on to fall short against Estonia in the final and as a result failed to end their 16-year wait for a competition title.

While every League D nation is guaranteed promotion at the end of play on Monday, with the division being completely abolished ahead of the 2028-29 campaign, Mindaugas Cepas’s men will certainly want to avoid finishing at the foot of the standings after facing Liechtenstein, who they have bizarrely beaten 2-0 in each of the previous three meetings between the sides.

Following a damning World Cup qualification campaign in which they lost all of their eight Group J games and failed to score a single goal, conceding a huge 31 in the process, Liechtenstein have also weathered a deflating set of Nations League fixtures.

Having been beaten 2-0 by Lithuania in their first match, Konrad Funfstuck’s men did well to steady the ship and play out a score draw with table-toppers Azerbaijan, but after falling to a slim defeat against Odlar Yurdu on Friday evening, the visitors head into Monday’s clash requiring victory by three goals in order to climb off the foot of the standings.

To do so, Blau-Rot will certainly have to discover some attacking threat though, having not won by more than a two-goal margin since October 2007 and at the moment in an extremely rough patch of form, losing 19 of their latest 21 outings in all competitions.

Although they do not boast the best record against Lithuania, losing six of their prior eight meetings with Trispalves, Liechtenstein do have experience of overcoming Monday’s hosts, beating them 2-0 at Rheinpark Stadion in June 2011.

Lithuania form (all competitions):.

Liechtenstein Nations League form:.

Liechtenstein form (all competitions):.

Having been shown a straight red card against Azerbaijan last month, 23-year-old forward Armandas Kucys will miss this week’s match for Lithuania and could be replaced by either Ignas Venckus or Edgaras Dubickas in attack.

After their victory against Blau-Rot last time out, it would be no surprise to see the hosts revert back to having three in midfield, with Lukas Michelbrink and Torino’s Gvidas Gineitis both likely to feature.

Although they kept a clean sheet with five in defence against Suriname on Thursday evening, it is likely that Trispalves deploy a back four this time out, with Justas Lasickas captaining the side from left-back.

Liechtenstein have a fully fit squad to choose from on Monday night as goalkeeper Tim-Tiado Oehri returns from a lengthy ACL injury and 19-year-old defender Yonas Abido receives his first call-up to the national side.

Hoping to net their first goal of the campaign in the final fixture, the only nation alongside Georgia still yet to have scored with one match remaining, Blau-Rot’s chances of ending their rut could well be down to Fabio Luque-Notaro and Alessandro Lo Russo, who are likely to form the visitors’ strike partnership this week.

Lithuania possible starting lineup:.

Bartkus; Sirvys, Kazukolovas, Utkus, Lasickas; Gineitis, Vorobjovas, Michelbrink; Jankauskas, Dubickas, Venckus.

Liechtenstein possible starting lineup:.

B.Buchel; N.Hasler, Weissenhofer, Traber, Goppel, Zund; Sele, M.Buchel, A.Hasler, Luque-Notaro, Saglam.

With nothing to lose, Liechtenstein will be gunning to end their Nations League campaign on a high and claim their first victory over Lithuania in 15 years.

However, facing a Trispalves side who have lost just one of their previous five matches and took all three points when the nations met in September, it is difficult to see that happening and we predict the hosts to confirm a second-placed finish by winning on Monday evening.

#2295. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

📅 18 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4993 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet.
  • In a recent development, in the end it also points to another thing.
  • What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In a recent development, in the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

It has been revealed that “It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously remarked of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

Sources indicate that that is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

Industry observers note that we have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Industry observers note that can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick stated this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

In a recent development, having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1.

Recent findings suggest that but beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

Industry observers note that united were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area highlighted the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm.

And that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick states he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”.

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick mentioned he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”.

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”.

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick noted. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”.

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

Sources indicate that “We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sunderland have been dealt a massive blow amid growing concerns about the latest news surrounding Brian Brobbey's injuries.

The 24-year-old withdrew from his national team squad shortly after leaving the Stadium of Light, with reports in the Netherlands warning he may have suffered a muscle tear.

While there has been no official diagnosis from the Black Cats' side, his absence earlier this season caused problems for Regis Le Bris, and could be set to do so again.

Former Sunderland chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Brobbey's absence will be a serious blow to Sunderland's chances of turning their season around.

They at the moment sit inside the Premier League's bottom three, with growing fears they could be sucked into a relegation battle, and need all their star players fit and firing.

Given Brobbey's role in Le Bris' side, and the amount he is relied upon to lead the line, the latest reports surrounding his fitness have set alarm bells ringing in the North East.

Brown warned Football Insider last month that Sunderland's growing injury list will leave them in "substantial trouble" if star players are forced to spend long spells on the sidelines.

The last international break saw both Brobbey and Dan Ballard fall victim to fresh injury blows, and this one has brought no more relief, with more casualties suffered.

News surrounding the striker's injury from the Netherlands has now set alarm bells ringing, and Sunderland's miserable start to the season could be set to continue.

"Losing Brian Brobbey will be a massive blow for Sunderland if he's out for a long time," Brown told Football Insider.

"They'll assess him, do scans and everything at Sunderland to get a better idea of how long he will miss, but if it's a serious injury, that's very bad news for their chances.

"Brobbey has shown this season how important he is, not just with the goals he's scored by his general play, leading the line and providing an outlet for them.

"He occupies defenders, he's not afraid of a battle and a fight, he'll run in behind, he can drop short, and he scores goals which Sunderland have been lacking for a while.

"All of a sudden, for them to miss that player, it leaves them short of options and it's a huge change to the way they're able to play.

"I don't see anybody in that squad who can step in and play that same role at such a high level, so as far as Sunderland are concerned, they'll be hoping it's only a minor issue.".

Should Sunderland's form take another hit in Brobbey's absence, questions are certain to be asked of Le Bris, regardless of whether he is the one at fault.

With the Black Cats already in the bottom three and in danger of being caught in a relegation scrap, the powers that be may be forced into making a drastic decision.

Brown told Football Insider on 2 November that Sunderland are reluctant to sack Le Bris, but are determined to see results improve as they strive towards their ambitious plans.

While there are mitigating circumstances, including major injuries which have limited Le Bris' side, there is a growing feeling that results must improve immediately.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada1,2,3. Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta2, the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

Sources indicate that a, Geological map of the early Precambrian rocks in the North China Craton94, showing the distribution of Archaean and Palaeoproterozoic rocks. b, Geological map of the Qian’an-Lulong area (modified after refs. 95,96,97), showing the spatial distribution of the early Archaean Muchangkou–Shimen Complex, which includes the Muchangkou Complex in the Huangbaiyu area and the Shimen Complex in the Labashan area16. c, Geological map of the Shimen Complex16. The complex is composed of Eoarchaean to Mesoarchaean granitoids and supracrustal rocks as enclaves of varying sizes in undeformed 2.5-Gyr-old potassic granite.

In a recent development, a, View of the hill showing the outcrop location of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss. b, The 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss is aligned parallel to the foliation in the 3.5-Gyr-old potassic granite gneiss and is intruded by 2.5-Gyr-old undeformed potassic granite. The locations of samples J2212, J2302 and J2303 are shown. c, 3.95-Gyr-old banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212). The light-coloured layers, commonly less than 1 cm in width, are considered to be deformed granitic veins. d, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302). e, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303). Compared with sample J2212, there are fewer veins in J2302 and J2303 and these were removed during sample preparation. f, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302) indicates a granoblastic texture and is composed of plagioclase, quartz and biotite, with minor microcline. g, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303) has a similar texture and mineral composition to J2302, except for containing less biotite. h, 3.95-Gyr-old banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212) consists of different components. The lower right contains more K-feldspar (monzogranitic layer) compared with the upper left (trondhjemitic layer), consistent with the banded characteristics in the field. Both layers show the same foliation defined by oriented biotite flakes.

a, 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (J2302). b, Trondhjemitic gneiss (J2303). c, Banded trondhjemitic gneiss (J2212, including zircons analysed in two sessions from the same sample, marked as J2212A and J2212B). On the left are CL images and on the right are secondary electron images. MA and RC identify magmatic and recrystallized domains, respectively, whereas R represents overgrowth rims and grains newly formed during metamorphism. The analytical sites are marked with white circles, together with the analysis number and age. Secondary electron images show that the weakly modified zircons retain euhedral prismatic shapes, a typical characteristic of magmatic zircon. This feature is particularly evident in zircons from sample J2303, which have been less affected by metamorphism.

Recent findings suggest that a, Zircon analyses of trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2302 define two concordant age groups at 3.95 Gyr and 3.45 Gyr, interpreted as the timing of magmatic crystallization and subsequent metamorphism, respectively. b, Most zircons in trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2303 are magmatic and cluster near 3.95 Gyr. Overgrowth rims show radiogenic Pb loss, including analysis 61.1R, which is the closest to concordia. c, Zircon analyses from banded trondhjemitic gneiss sample J2212 (including zircons analysed in two sessions from the same sample, marked as J2212A and J2212B) are more scattered, with the main population along a discordia line from 3.95 Gyr. However, several zircons with magmatic zoning yield concordant ages of 3.86–3.70 Gyr, potentially owing to the intrusion of thin granitic veins and/or partial resetting of the U–Pb system of 3.95-Gyr-old zircons. Analysis 63.1MA in J2212B has the oldest 207Pb/206Pb age of 3,989 ± 10 Myr but indicates slightly reverse discordance, probably because of local enrichment of radiogenic Pb during later metamorphism98. d, Concordia diagram of all samples for analyses with <20% discordance. The weighted mean 207Pb/206Pb age of 3,951 ± 3 Myr (95% confidence level, MSWD = 1.15, n = 33) for magmatic/recrystallized cores is considered the best estimate for the magmatic crystallization age of the trondhjemitic gneiss protolith.

Zircon Lu–Hf isotope analyses were carried out in two sessions. Circles and triangles represent the results of the first analyses and squares represent the results of the second analytical session. All of the magmatic/recrystallized zircons with >3.9-Gyr 207Pb/206Pb age have homogeneous 176Hf/177Hf ratios except for J2302-2.1MA, which has a high 176Lu/177Hf ratio. The magmatic/recrystallized zircons with <3.9-Gyr 207Pb/206Pb age in samples J2302 and J2303 are all located near the Pb loss line. Some newly formed zircons have much higher 176Hf/177Hf ratios, which may be related to external fluids introduced during metamorphism.

a–c, REE patterns of zircons from the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (samples J2302, J2303 and J2212, respectively). The REE data were filtered using the methods suggested in ref. 26. d,e, Magmatic oxygen fugacity and H2O content of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss. The oxygen fugacity (fO2) was calculated using the oxybarometer proposed in ref. 82 based on the average REE content of the filtered magmatic zircons. The magmatic water content was calculated using the hygrometer established in ref. 26 and the effect of U loss in the whole rock was corrected assuming a Th/U ratio of 5 (ref. 26). Considering that the composition of sample J2212 may have been influenced by alteration and the intrusion of thin younger veins, the average composition of J2302 and J2303 was used for calculating the fO2 and water content of J2212.

a, An–Ab–Or diagram99. Note that sample J2212 plots in the granite field owing to the presence of thin younger granitic veins. The homogeneous 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss (samples J2302 and J2303) is similar to the granitoids in Anshan and Nuvvuagittuq (mainly trondhjemitic gneiss) but different from those in Acasta, Tarim and Greenland (mainly tonalitic and granodioritic gneisses). b, Nb versus Ta diagram. c, Sr versus Y diagram. and d, La/Yb versus Yb classification diagrams for high-pressure, medium-pressure and low-pressure TTGs4. The 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss consistently plots in the high-pressure TTG field, being similar to the 3.72-Gyr-old Aktash gneiss in the Tarim Craton and some TTG rocks in Greenland but different from many other ≥3.8-Gyr-old granitoids around the world, which mostly plot into the medium-pressure and low-pressure TTG fields. Several samples from the literature that plot outside the ranges in b and d are not shown.

a,b, LILE contents of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss and potential source rocks (Supplementary Tables 6 and 7). The dashed red lines represent LILE contents required for the source to produce the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss by 7%, 10%, 20% and 30% melting, assuming that these elements are perfectly incompatible with bulk partition coefficient equal to 0. Considering that the degree of partial melting of a mafic rock source needs to be >7% for melt aggregation to form magma but <30% to match the high SiO2 contents of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss, the LILE contents of the source need to be in the grey shaded area. Because the sources of Eoarchaean TTGs are from mafic rocks, we have compiled the geochemical data of Eoarchaean mafic rocks worldwide (Methods and Supplementary Table 7). Comparing the LILE contents of these mafic rocks with those required to form the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss, the amphibolite group I in Acasta is the most suitable source to use for modelling, consistent with the fact that it is the only mafic rock >3.95 Gyr old. c, P–T pseudosection for the composition of amphibolite group I from Acasta, assuming X(H2O) = 1.5 wt% and Fe3+/(Fe3+ + Fe2+) ratio = 0.1. The dashed white lines represent the wt% of melt.

a–d, The red dot denotes the median sodic TTG composition4, which was assumed as the starting melt composition. Solid black and orange curves represent the effects of fractional crystallization of plagioclase and hornblende, respectively, whereas dashed black and orange curves represent the effects of accumulation of plagioclase and hornblende, respectively. Orange squares show the compositions of the 3.95-Gyr-old high-pressure TTGs from this study. Small dots represent melts produced by partial melting of the Acasta amphibolite group I (Supplementary Table 9), colour-coded by pressure. Comparison indicates that plagioclase accumulation and hornblende fractional crystallization can explain the positive Eu and Sr anomalies in our samples (a,b) but they fail to simultaneously reproduce the high (La/Yb)N and (Gd/Yb)N ratios and the high SiO2 contents observed in the rocks (c,d). By contrast, melts formed under high-pressure conditions match well with the main geochemical characteristics of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic samples.

Sources indicate that the positive εHf(t) values of magmatic zircons from the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss indicate that its basaltic precursor was young juvenile crust derived from a DMD. Even if the basaltic precursor (assuming 176Lu/177Hf = 0.022) was derived from a 4.5-Gyr-old DMD with a similar 176Lu/177Hf ratio (0.0384) to modern depleted mantle, its extraction time from the mantle could not be earlier than 4.0 Ga (solid blue line). If the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss was formed by partial melting of basalt immediately extracted from a DMD with similar 176Lu/177Hf ratio, then the timing of mantle depletion can be estimated to be about 4.35 Ga (dashed black line). Earlier depletion of the mantle is required if partial melting of a basaltic precursor occurred some time after its extraction from a DMD (dashed blue line) or the degree of depletion in the mantle is less than modern depleted mantle (dashed red line). If the basaltic precursor was derived from a possible ultra-depleted mantle proposed by some researchers100, the depletion can be slightly delayed. Nevertheless, the depletion still needs to be no later than 4.2 Ga even if the 176Lu/177Hf of the ultra-depleted mantle is as high as 0.041 (solid purple line). Therefore, a Hadean DMD is necessary to yield the Hf isotope composition of the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss.

Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai has confirmed that he was close to suffering an injury while playing for Hungary.

The Reds star was part of the Hungarian XI that beat Georgia 2-0 in the Nations League on Saturday, registering an assist.

Many Reds fans were worried about the 26-year-old's fitness given Andoni Iraola had expressed concern about a potential injury heading into the international break.

It has been revealed that szoboszlai fuelled those fears after admitting he was close to pulling out of Saturday's match, telling reporters: "During the warm-up I was close to saying that I wouldn't be able to play after all. I felt the injury during one of my shots, but I thought to myself that, having come this far, I wasn't going to let the team down.

Recent findings suggest that "So I tried to give everything I had, as best as I could. My leg felt good, but now the treatment process starts all over again, and I need to be ready for Tuesday.".

Szoboszlai has struggled hamstring and knee issues this season, and Liverpool will want him to sit out of his nation's clash with Northern Ireland on Tuesday given the Reds will face Manchester United in the Premier League on November 22.

While Szoboszlai has not played particularly well this season for the Reds, he is one of just three senior options for midfield.

Losing him for an extended period of time would leave Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch as the only experienced stars for Iraola to choose from, but the latter has not been trusted by the head coach in 2026-27.

Though youngster Trey Nyoni should arguably be in the Reds' starting XI irrespective of injury concerns, the 19-year-old cannot be expected to start on a consistent basis.

Given Szoboszlai has already suffered two injuries this campaign, further minutes this international break would be a major concern ahead of the busy winter period.

With depth a serious glitch for Iraola, it should come as no surprise to see the club linked to midfielders ahead of the January transfer window.

Lamine Camara has often been touted as a target for the Merseysiders, and his abilities with and without the ball would make him a strong addition.

The 22-year-old would ensure that Nyoni is not overplayed, while also allowing Szoboszlai to avoid being forced into the XI should his injury complications persist.

Whether Liverpool act on any interest in January remains to be seen, but it would be risky to head into the rest of the campaign with the same options in midfield.

Thomas Frank has been revealed as Crystal Palace's next manager.

The former Brentford and Tottenham boss has come into Selhurst Park with plenty to do, and much to turn around.

The Dane is taking over the Eagles when they are sitting at the bottom of the Premier League, with the goal undoubtedly to climb out of those relegation positions.

As well as continuing with their journey into the latter stages of the Europa League.

Frank will have plenty of decisions to make, with the potential for new chances to emerge for the fringe players in Palace's squad,.

With Frank likely to make plenty of changes, these three need to be first on his list of priorities.

Frank is a manager who has used three-at-the-back in the past, and it is one of the common formations he uses.

However, he is also fond of using the 4-2-3-1 as well.

At Brentford and Tottenham, he often swapped between the two, but at Crystal Palace, their lack of central defensive options makes it tougher to sustain it.

In the squad, there are only four fit natural centre-backs, with Jaydee Canvot, Chris Richards, Axel Disasi and Honest Ahanor.

The latter also barely featured this season, with three appearances.

With three centre-backs needed each game, and European football this season, it is not ideal for 75 per cent of your options to be used up each matchday.

Making a change to a four-man defence makes a lot of sense.

Speaking of Crystal Palace's defence, with one centre-back dropping out, Frank will have a decision to make.

And it should be Disasi dropping out of the team.

As per FotMob, he has been on the poorer side in winning duels, coming in at the 32nd percentile with 54.1 per cent for total duels won.

While for aerial duels, he comes in the 30th percentile, with just a 53.8 per cent win rate.

A partnership of Richards and Canvot may ultimately be the best option for the Eagles, with the American having a 63.2 per cent success rate in duels, and the Frenchman with 60 per cent.

Daichi Kamada has been having a good season for Crystal Palace, even if the Eagles have not.

The Japanese midfielder has one goal and three assists in 10 Premier League games, and his influence has been clear.

Kamada may be better played centrally, rather than in those wide number 10 positions he has often been deployed in.

Kamada ranks in the 93rd percentile for line-breaking passes with 84 this season, showing he can consistently play passes that break the opponent's structure.

And doing so is much easier from a central role.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A member of the coaching staff at Hull City has spoken very highly of what Lewis Koumas was like behind the scenes during his loan move at the MKM Stadium.

The Liverpool striker spent the second half of last season with the Tigers, playing a part in their promotion to the Premier League with three goals in 18 Championship appearances (including the play-offs).

He’s since become a fixed first-team player at Anfield, being handed five starts among his 14 appearances across all competitions and scoring in the Champions League victory over LASK in October.

Hull assistant coach Dean Holden spoke to The Redmen TV about how Koumas immediately won people over with his humility and hardworking attitude.

The 47-year-old said: “Within a week, everyone fell in love with him, from Stan on the door, the security guy, to the kitchen staff, kit men, the lot. We all fell in love with him.

According to recent reports, “You know why? Just because he’s a real humble lad who just wants to be the best he can be and affects people around him in an energetic manner and just loves football.”.

Holden went on to share anecdotes of Koumas being out on the training pitch along with Joe Gelhardt ’20 minutes out before everyone else is in the gym’, telling coaches not to ‘sugarcoat’ advice to him, and waiting patiently for his mother to collect him after he scored a late winner for Hull on his debut against Blackburn instead of ‘going out on the town and celebrating’.

Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

While we’re sure that the Liverpool youngster has been helped by sage advice from his father Jason, who graced the Premier League with West Brom and Wigan, the onus is still on him to put all of that bequeathed wisdom into action, and he’s most certainly doing that.

Andoni Iraola clearly has plenty of faith in the 21-year-old if he’s playing him regularly, even starting him against Manchester City (albeit that Alexander Isak wasn’t fit), and the young striker is repaying that trust with his performances on the pitch.

John Aldridge voiced his belief that the Wales international will ‘play for Liverpool for a long time‘, with Koumas standing out for his indefatigable pressing in the final third, which carries echoes of the beloved Bobby Firmino.

The stories shared by Holden testify to the tremendous attitude of the Reds youngster, who’s remained grounded and earned his place in the first-team squad to the extent that he’s nudged Federico Chiesa further down the pecking order.

We’re sure there’s still so much more to come from the Welshman, provided he can maintain the traits which have taken him this far already and (fingers crossed) avoid any major injury issues.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER and CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:03 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 16:48 EST, 14 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel was dragged into a bitter race row on the eve of England's Nations League showdown with Spain.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols in case their players suffered racist abuse at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday evening.

England players were notoriously subject to racial abuse at the Bernabeu in 2004 and England have not played in Madrid since.

But Spain manager Luis de la Fuente reacted angrily when he was told that Tuchel had addressed the subject.

Sources indicate that 'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente stated. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'.

The row then deepened when a Spanish journalist told Tuchel about De La Fuente's reaction and the England coach grew exasperated with the line of questioning.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols.

Sources indicate that 'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente noted. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'.

'I was polite enough to answer a question from your colleagues,' Tuchel remarked, 'and you run and ask Spain's coach and tell them that I talked about racism in Spain.

'I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered a question politely. I never expect racism. The dressing room is the most anti-racist place in the world. This is a perfect example of how you create confusion out of nothing.'.

It has been revealed that tuchel had earlier stated: 'It's notable that the players know about the protocol. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.

Industry observers note that 'We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]. There is a protocol in place.'.

England midfielder Declan Rice remarked that Tuchel had not yet addressed the group about racism protocols but that they were clear about what they would do if any England players were abused.

England's game against Bulgaria in Sofia in 2019 was halted after allegations of racism against England players but the game was completed.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that James Trafford will face world champions Spain on Sunday night, raising questions over Jordan Pickford’s status as England’s No 1.

It was assumed that Pickford, who the head coach maintains is his first choice, would keep the jersey given the identity of the opposition and the chance for England to top their Nations League group with victory here in Madrid.

However, Tuchel will hand Leeds stopper Trafford his fifth cap at the Metropolitano Stadium.

Industry observers note that ’We want to try and see how far Traff is,’ remarked Tuchel, who rotated his keepers during last month’s international break. ‘So he gets a highly competitive match. We had some changes in the back four in the last match (2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday), so we went for more stability and more experience with Pickers.

‘Tomorrow is a high-pressure match, on the biggest stage, and it's exactly what we need to see where we are with him (Trafford). Hopefully he's not too over-excited or overly nervous, because there's no need to be. We trust him. But it is different to play for England than to play for your club.

'To have the opportunity to play matches where it really matters is the best way to show up, and to show that you're ready.’.

It was put to Tuchel that it would make more sense to play the goalkeeper he believes is his No 1 in the biggest game from this round of fixtures.

’It was the circumstances of the last match, that we had some changes in the back four, and that was the decision in the goalkeeping team,’ he stated. 'Jordan is at the moment our No.1. I have a very clear picture in high-pressure moments. He played in tournaments and played for me in the World Cup.’.

Meanwhile, centre back Ezri Konsa is also set to start after recovering from a knee problem.

‘I’m very pleased with how he has fitted in seamlessly at Arsenal,’ mentioned Tuchel. ‘It just looks like he's always been there. For us, it’s amazing that he plays on the highest level, competes for every title, is in an atmosphere and in a situation where it really matters that you stay focused and you show up every three days. It's only positives for us.’.

PROBABLE ENGLAND XI: Trafford; White, Quansah, Konsa, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Jude Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.

Spain's penalty and Elliot Anderson's red card should have been overturned during England's 3-2 Nations League victory.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that Jarell Quansah was fouled in the build-up to the game's most contentious moment.

In the 63rd minute, the game was flipped on its head, as Clement Turpin was left with no other choice but to send off Anderson.

Just before he pushed Lamine Yamal over in the box, though, Quansah had been dispossessed near the halfway line, allowing a quick Spanish break.

As Hackett pointed out previously, the Manchester City man could have avoided a red card by simply making a genuine attempt for the ball.

Either way, the situation probably should have been avoided, with the Three Lions deserving of a free-kick for the foul on Quansah by Yamal.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett that, while England deserved a free-kick, at least the referee was consistent with his decisions.

According to recent reports, "There's no getting away from it; that is a foul. However you look at it, in trying attempting to play the ball, it's also the man," he stated.

According to recent reports, "So it's a very easy foul. Football's a contact sport, and I think this is where the debate comes in. Given this referee and his skill set, he's not going come in on that.

Industry observers note that "He's not going to give that. And because his, if you like, guide, his line of interference is much higher. Then he will say football is a contact sport and therefore it's okay to carry on.

"If you're in the local park refereeing, you're gonna give that as a foul. Look, England fans can complain.

"The reality is the same should have happened with Anderson. If you're going to give that, then you've got to give the foul from Anderson [on Marc Cucurella].".

On the two big decisions, Turpin was definitely consistent, but he let a few other things slide - ones that should have been called back, and vice versa.

Yamal was at the centre of multiple battles during the game, often throwing himself to the floor to win a cheap free-kick.

Industry observers note that in the first half, the same happened up against Anderson. The Man City star won the ball cleanly, but because Yamal fell to the ground, a free-kick brought a halt to England's attack.

The referee also fell for Fabian Ruiz's play-acting in the penalty area, awarding Spain a free-kick after tussling with Anthony Gordon at a set-piece.

Estonia will welcome Bulgaria to the Lillekula Stadium in Tallinn for Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The hosts, who have secured a top-two finish, could still achieve automatic promotion, while the visitors only have pride to play for on the final matchday of the league phase.

Having been in the bottom two tiers for all five editions of the Nations League, Estonia have put themselves in a position to win promotion to League B for the very first time.

Jurgen Henn's side are guaranteed at least a promotion playoff spot after winning the draw and drawing three of their five matches in Group 4C.

In fact, they have recorded four consecutive shutouts since playing out a 1-1 draw with Iceland on the first matchday.

Their latest clean sheet enabled them to pick up a 1-0 victory in Saturday's away clash against Luxembourg, which came courtesy of Maksim Paskotsi's second goal of the 2026-27 Nations League campaign.

Sitting in second spot and two points adrift of Iceland, Estonia know they need a win and Luxembourg to claim three points in Reykjavik if they are to snatch automatic promotion on the final matchday.

That would require Estonia to pick up their first-ever win against Bulgaria, having drawn two and lost one of their previous three meetings.

Bulgaria already know they will be competing in League C next time around after falling hopelessly short in their promotion bid, mustering just four points from their five matches in Group C4.

After taking just a point from their first three games, Bulgaria finally ended their five-game winless run in all internationals with a 2-0 away victory over Luxembourg in their final outing of the September/October international break.

However, they failed to build upon that result in their most recent outing against Iceland, as they slumped to a demoralising 5-0 defeat in Plovdiv, ensuring they will end the league phase without a home win to their name.

While they cannot finish any higher than third, the Lions are still at risk of dropping to the bottom of the group, with just a point separating them from Luxembourg in fourth position.

Bulgaria may be unbeaten in three meetings against Estonia, but they had to settle for a goalless draw in their only previous away encounter in European Championship qualifying in April 2003.

Their hopes of troubling the scorers on this occasion may be tempered by the fact they have failed to score in three of their last four outings, including a stalemate in September's reverse fixture between these two nations.

Estonia form (all competitions):.

Bulgaria form (all competitions):.

Henn could opt for consistency by naming the same lineup that started Friday's narrow win over Luxembourg.

Friday's match-winner Paskotsi will feature alongside Erko Tougjas and Karol Mets in central defence, while Rasmus Peetson and Michael Schjonning-Larsen are set to operate as the two wing-backs.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Patrik Kristal will lead the line with Mattias Mannilaan, who is aiming to bring his club form to the international stage after netting five goals in his last four games for Kalju.

As for the visitors, they are unable to call upon Martin Minchev, who withdrew from the squad last week due to injury.

With Ribarski likely to make alterations, Ivan Turitsov and Dimitar Velkovski are in contention to feature in the backline on Monday.

Martin Petkov, Ivaylo Chochev and Georgi Lazarov are also among those who could come into Ribarski's thinking.

Estonia possible starting lineup:.

Hein; Peetson, Paskotsi, Tougjas, Mets, Schjonning-Larsen; Kait, Palumets, Shein; Mannilaan, Kristal.

Bulgaria possible starting lineup:.

Naumov; Turitsov, Velkov, Tsenov, Velkovski; Kraev, Gruev; L Petkov, Chochev, M Petkov; Lazarov.

Estonia have proven to be a tough team to break down in Group C4, and considering Bulgaria have failed to score in three of their last four games, we think the hosts could edge a cagey contest on Monday.
